# Decision history — pixelkit

Every revision of every decision, plus the terminal revisions of other normative records. Includes archived records: this is the project's memory of what it used to think.

## pixelkit.decision.device-pixel-rects

### Revision 1 — Controls take device-pixel rectangles; Theme sizes are logical and scaled by the control

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.decision.device-pixel-rects/1` · scope `path "README.md"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-shell/src/scale.rs"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/**"`, `path "crates/liminalkit/**"` · topic `units`

Every Rect a Ui control or the Painter takes is in device pixels, the same pixels the buffer holds and the pointer reports. Layout is written in logical pixels and converted once at the call site: Ui::px for a length, Ui::rect for a rectangle, Scale::rect for a whole logical layout (edges rounded independently so neighbours keep touching). Theme's dimensional tokens (padding, row_height, corner_radius, border_width, focus_width) are logical and every control passes them through Ui::px when it uses them. Theme's two font styles are the exception: Ui::new converts its own copy to device pixels so measurement and drawing share one text-cache key, and Ui::text_style converts a custom style.

**Context.** The README said coordinates given to Ui were logical while the examples converted with Scale::px and the painter worked on device pixels. Inside the ui crate the stated contract (theme tokens logical) was applied inconsistently: dropdown and toast scaled row_height and padding, while surface, panel, table, tabs, badge, text_field and the form controls used them raw, so panels and tables shrank at HiDPI scales.

**Consequences.** At scale 1.0 nothing changes. At other scales, panels, table rows, borders and corner radii now follow the scale. A downstream screen that reads ui.theme.row_height still gets a logical value and scales it itself, as the dropdown instructions in the README already assumed. The ui gallery example takes a scale factor so the contract can be eyeballed at 2x.

## pixelkit.decision.facade-crate-and-app-adapter

### Revision 1 — A top-level `liminalkit` crate is the entry point: re-exports, App/Screen adapter, and the cross-crate examples

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.decision.facade-crate-and-app-adapter/1` · scope `path "Cargo.toml"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/Cargo.toml"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-windowing/Cargo.toml"`, `path "crates/liminalkit/**"` · topic `entry-point`

crates/liminalkit is the front door. It re-exports the six component crates as liminalkit::{raster, text, shell, ui, windowing} (kms behind a `kms` feature), offers a prelude, and adds liminalkit::app: a Screen trait (one required method, draw(&mut Ui, &mut Context)) and an App<S: Screen> that implements PixelApp, owning the TextCache, RasterKernel, Input, Focus and TouchPointer, forwarding every host event, attaching Tab traversal, and calling Input::end_frame. Context carries the frame's requests back to the host (exit, title, fullscreen, cursor, IME caret, reset_focus). PixelApp stays the low-level interface and App's source is its worked example. Examples that need more than one crate (hello, window, window_lowlevel, panes, multi, touch, touch_tuning) live in crates/liminalkit/examples behind required-features = ["test-fonts"]; the dev-dependency cycle between liminalkit-ui and liminalkit-windowing is gone. Features test-fonts, accessibility and kms forward to the component crates.

**Context.** A first-time user had to assemble a painter, text cache, input, kernel, scale and theme and forward six events before drawing a button. The review asked for an optional high-level adapter that keeps the low-level interfaces intact, and for the cross-crate examples to leave the two crates that dev-depended on each other.

**Consequences.** App does not publish an accessibility tree, arbitrate touch gestures beyond forwarding the first contact as a pointer press, or open further windows; a screen that needs those implements PixelApp. Workspace path dependencies now carry a version requirement and every crate has a description and repository, which costs nothing now and is required later if the crates are ever published; publishing itself is not decided.

## pixelkit.decision.popups-claim-input-first

### Revision 1 — Anything that floats claims its input before the background draws and is drawn last

`proposed` · `@pixelkit.decision.popups-claim-input-first/1` · scope `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/src/dropdown.rs"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/src/menu.rs"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/src/overlay.rs"`, `path "crates/liminalkit-ui/src/tooltip.rs"`, `path "crates/liminalkit/src/app.rs"` · topic `popups`

Dropdown, Menu and Overlay share one contract. The screen owns the popup's state. At the start of the frame, before the Ui is built and before Focus::handle_tab reads the keys, the popup's handle_input takes the clicks, context clicks, scroll and keys that belong to it or that land outside it (Input::take_keys, restored later with Input::restore_keys, which does not start a new interaction epoch), so background controls never act through a popup. At the end of the frame its draw paints it above everything, hands the retained keys to its own controls, and reports what happened. Under App this split is Screen::before_frame and the tail of Screen::draw. A modal Overlay keeps its own Focus so Tab is trapped inside it; a popover is dismissed by an outside click that is swallowed rather than delivered.

**Context.** Immediate mode has no z-order. The dropdown already drew last and claimed first; adding menus, dialogs and popovers each with their own arrangement would have given screens three rules to remember.

**Consequences.** A popup that is drawn without a prior handle_input still works but is not modal for that frame: draw claims what is left. Overlay content registers its controls with the overlay's Focus explicitly (the _focused control variants); the background Focus may also see them register, harmlessly, because the keys it would act on were taken.
